title: Overfitting and honest generalization estimates
learning_objectives: Explain why training performance can improve while unseen-data performance worsens.
Separate training, validation, and final test roles.
Recognize data leakage and repeated test-set tuning.

misconceptions.description: The model with the lowest training error must generalize best.
It is harmless to repeatedly tune choices against the final test set.

critical_errors.description: Claims that training-set performance is an unbiased estimate of unseen-data performance.
Recommends using final test results repeatedly for model selection without disclosing leakage.

teaching_brief.goal: Help the learner connect overfitting to reuse of finite data and distinguish dataset roles.
teaching_brief.learner_profile: A beginner who selects models by training accuracy.
instructions: Explain training, validation, and final test data as different information boundaries.
Ask what changes when the test set is consulted repeatedly.
Include one remedy without implying that any remedy guarantees generalization.
prohibited_disclosures: Do not reveal held-out item wording.
Do not claim cross-validation eliminates every source of bias.

pretest.prompt: A complex model reaches 100% training accuracy but 62% accuracy on new data. What is the likely problem?

choices.text: Overfitting to training-specific patterns
The new data automatically became training data
Training accuracy must be wrong because it is high
Generalization is defined by training accuracy

pretest.prompt: What is the proper role of a final test set?

choices.text: Tune every hyperparameter against it.
Provide a final estimate after model choices are fixed.
Train the model on it before evaluation.
Replace the training set.

posttest.prompt: Why can repeated tuning against a test set make its reported performance optimistic?

choices.text: Model-selection decisions indirectly adapt to chance features of that test set.
The test labels become physically larger.
Optimizers cannot use validation data.
A test set has no sampling variability.

posttest.prompt: Which split should normally guide hyperparameter choice while preserving a final holdout?

choices.text: Validation data or cross-validation within the development data
The final test set after every training epoch
Only the easiest training examples
No data at all

transfer.prompt: A feature is calculated using information recorded after the prediction target occurred. What risk does this create?

choices.text: Target or temporal leakage that will not be available at real prediction time
Guaranteed fairness
A larger true sample
Automatic causal identification

transfer.prompt: Five hundred model variants are tried and only the best validation score is reported. What should be considered?

choices.text: Selection over many variants can exploit validation noise; independent confirmation is valuable.
Trying more variants guarantees the selected score is unbiased.
Validation data becomes identical to the population.
Model selection cannot overfit.

retention.prompt: Overfitting is best detected by a gap between...

choices.text: development performance and honest performance on unseen data
two identical copies of the training score
the model name and file name
the number of labels and the color palette

retention.prompt: After all model and hyperparameter choices are fixed, which data should estimate final generalization?

choices.text: A held-out test set not used for those choices
The training set alone
The test set used repeatedly during tuning
Only misclassified training points
